translation: Šalim-Aššur and Šu-Bēlum son of Iddin-abum settled accounts before us, and Šalim-Aššur set down 1 talent 13 minas of bad copper as a claim on Šu-Bēlum. Šalim-Aššur said to Šu-Bēlum: On the orders of Issu-arik, my father, I wrote myself as your father's guarantor. I took silver from his outstanding claims and paid to cover his debt, and I paid a great deal of silver from my joint-stock capital for your father's debt. Come! Let me show you my tablets!" Šu-Bēlum answered: "Why do you inform only me? Sue me together with my brothers." Witnessed by Puzur-Aššur, by Ennānum. The Kanesh colony gave us for these proceedings and we gave (our testimony) before the dagger of Aššur. "

transliteration: kunuk <PN>Aššur-emūqī</PN> kunuk <PN>Ennam-Aššur</PN> mer'a <PN>Menā</PN> kunuk <PN>Iddin-abim</PN> ša ḫubul <PN>Iddin-abim</PN> 13 <PN>Mana</PN> kaspam ṣarrupam ištu ḫamuštem ša <PN>Qarwiā</PN> ana 36 ḫamšātem išaqqal <PN>Šuma</PN> lā išqul 1½ šiqil ina warḫem ana manā'em uṣṣab ša <PN>Amur-Ištar</PN> u <PN>Aššur-imittī</PN>
translation: Seal of Aššur-emūqi, seal of Ennam-Aššur son of Menaya, seal of Iddin-abum. Concerning the debt of Iddin-abum of 13 minas of refined silver. Reckoned from the week of Karriya he must pay within 36 weeks. If he has not paid (in time), he must pay interest at the rate 1½ shekel per month per mina. Concerning Amur-Ištar and Aššur-imittī.

translation: From Ikūn-pīya to Ennam-Aššur, Iddin-abum and Lā-qēp: Ennam-Aššur brings you 10 minas of silver under my seal. In addition to 40 minas of tin which Ennam-Aššur will send, add my silver and buy worth 2 minas of his tin - in addition to the one mina, and until you will make purchases for me ..., set aside the tin and send it as soon as possible. Until my servant arrives, with the rest of my silver make a profitable purchase of good from Talhat, (and) soft and send them to me. His donkeys ... per year together with my customers ...

translation: To Kurub-Ištar, Ikūn-piya, Šu-Ištar, Adida and Amur-Ištar from Šalim-Aššur; specifically to Kurub-Ištar: My dear brother and lord, the lapis lazuli that was the votive offering to Aššur has been lost. You and your caravan must listen to the tablet with the verdict of the City assembly, assist the attorney and the servant, and search Enna-Suen's goods in accordance with the verdict of the City, and if the lapis lazuli appears, then place it under seal and return the lapis lazuli and Enna-Suen in accordance with the verdict of the City. According to the verdict of the City wherever the attorney interrogates, he may impose an oath and search the goods. Also, if anyone has departed with an express caravan, the attorney will travel and search the goods of the express caravan. My dear brothers and lords, save me while I can still be saved. Do this favour for Aššur and for me.

transliteration: 1⅔ <PN>Mana</PN> 5 šiqil kaspam kunnukī ša <PN>Šu-Ḫubur</PN> ana <PN>Al-aḫim</PN> ezibu kīma <PN>Aššur-bēl-šaduē</PN> kaspam <PN>Annina</PN> ilqe <PN>Šuma</PN> ana kaspam anniem <PN>Maman</PN> ana <PN>Al-aḫim</PN> itu''ar <PN>Annina</PN> mer'a <PN>Puzur-Anna</PN> ubbabšu maḫar <PN>Aššur-bānī</PN> mer'a <PN>Kudāya</PN> maḫar <PN>Ilī-bānī</PN> mer'a <PN>Amur-Ištar</PN>
translation: Concerning the 1⅔ mina 5 shekels of sealed silver that Šu-hubur left with Ali-ahum - Annina has received the silver on behalf of Aššur-bēl-šadu'e. If anyone raises claim against Ali-ahum for this silver, Annina son of Puzur-Anna will clear him. Witnessed by Aššur-bāni son of Kutaya, by Ilī-bāni son of Amur-Ištar.

translation: To Ennam-Aššur from Lā-qēp: I and Ennānum entered your storeroom and brought out your bronze and the tablets, and they are in Itūr-ilī's house. Do not worry at all. Also, Šalim-Aššur ... the votive offering ... My journey to the City is approaching. If any silver has fallen into your hands, send it to your representatives so they can sell it on credit and I can do you a service. Send me word whether or not any silver has fallen into your hands. If I do not depart, do not be angry with me. Take care to send me word.

translation: 2 minas of silver, the agreed amount of his certified tablet, 12 shekels and 2 fine suppū-sheep, its interest, owed by happi-ahšu son of Zilpuriya.

translation: The judges passed the following verdict: The 6 shekels of silver that Kapsiya, wife of Ali-abum, had given to Būṣi, wife(?) of Iddin-Adad, and for which from the eponymy of Aššur-imittī, the boatman, she would add an interest of ½ mina per mina per year - for this silver and the accumulated interest on it Kapsiya, the wife of Ali-abum will sue Būṣi, wife (?) of Iddin-Adad. Akiya, son of Puzur-Aššur, Šamaš-bāni, son of Ennam-Suen, (and) Mannum-kī-Aššur, son of Ahu-waqar - these gentlemen were the judges.

translation: Seal of Ilī-nādā, son of Baziya, seal of Ennam-Ašsur, son of Kariya(?), seal of Kitaya, that [Kitaya] will manage ½ mina of silver belonging to Elamma. He is held by the silver. If he goes away to somewhere else, he will charge him 1 shekel per month.

translation: To Issu-arik from Šalim-Aššur: I made our guest Amuraya and our sister, the priestess, pay 1⅓ mina of refined silver, the proceeds from your carnelian, and Dudu is bringing it to you under my seal. 2½ minas ½ shekel owed by I..., x ½ mina owed by Kuzāzum, ½ mina owed by Aššur-bēl-awātim, all this, refined silver, from the proceeds of your carnelian, from these men, Dudu will bring to you in hahhum. 2 minas less 3 shekels is your silver, 5 shekels belong to me. Also, 2 ... and 2 shekels ... Imdī-ilum brought you 2 minas 3 shekels including its transport tariff. About the 7 minas of refined silver, the proceeds of your carnelian - if he has taken interest from your merchant, then in accordance with the tablet of ... let Dudu credit you for the price. 3½ shekels of gold ore sealed by me as a shipment is being brought to you by Dudu. 2½ shekels of gold Ani... the servant ... My dear father, take care and ship my goods to me, and ... May a final report from you come as soon as possible.

translation: We broke the seals for 4 minas of silver that Amur-Šamaš sent, and (discovered that) 4⅓ shekels of silver were missing.

translation: Seal of Šu-Kūbum, seal of Šu-Ištar, seal of Amur-Ištar, that, when his tin comes up (from Assur) Elamma will send 2 talents of tin to Šu-Ištar in Burušhattum and that Šu-Ištar will deliver in full to him 1 shekel (of silver) per (shekel of tin) above the current rate of exchange and that he will pay purified silver on the arrival of his tin.

translation: To Sūaya and Ennam-Aššur. Seal of Aššur-idī.

translation: [15 shekels of silver] Ennam-Aššur gave to Uṣur-<pī>-Aššur. If in the City a tablet with the seal of Uṣur-pī-Aššur <in the City> their sister Ummī-Išhara <has / shows>, to the effect that he will not claim what her mother Lamassutum had inherited and what had been left behind by her, then Uṣur-pī-Aššur will give back the 15 shekels of silver. In the presence of Ēnah-ilī, of Šalim-Ištar of Aššur-[... ... ...] of Mas(s)āya, of Aššur-mālik

translation: 8½ shekels of silver due from Ennānum, the blacksmith; 1 shekel of silver for buying bread I gave to you; 3 / 4 shekel of bad quality (silver) I gave you. Thereof you have given me 10 minas of wool and 5 shekels of tin.

translation: Thus Aššur-šad-ilī, Amur-Ištar, Ṭāb-ṣilli-Aššur, Ilī-anum, Anuppiya, and Ababayai, say to Kuliya: We have settled your affair concerning Sabasiya's house, includeing the setting of a term for you. And in addition to the silver and gold you had left behind we borrowed 1⅓ mina from Ṭāb-Aššur, son of Ṭāb-ilī, at an interest of 7 shekels per mina. And with that silver we have satisfied them, whereupon they released to us 3 tablets of the City (and) 1 tablet recording a debt of yours of 1½ mina of silver. Your wife has sealed (the debt-note) together with us, (dated to) the IVth month of the eponymy of Dān-Ea. Please, as soon as you have heard the letters, send the silver with the interest on it and then we will cancel the tablet with our seals and the seal of your wife. In accordance with your written instructions we seized Išme-Adad, son of Itūraya, and told him: You brought 5 minas of silver, meant for making purchases, belonging to Puzur-Aššur, son of Ahu-waqar. Confirm our claim on it, then it is you who can make the purchases and we will establish our claim on them. If the silver turns out to belong to Puzur-Aššur, Kuliya can take it." He answered: "Puzur-Aššur is in no way involved and I did not bring along any silver!" We led him down to the Gate of the god and in the Gate this agreement was reached: "Henceforth, wherever you see him you will make him swear the oath." As for Aššur-rēṣī, son of Innāya, their affair still rests and we have not obtained a written document and (hence) we continue to detain him."

translation: To Ali-ahum, Annina and Aššur-malik from Zukuwa: x minas of silver, its import duty added, and x+½ shekel from votive offerings, under seal, Šu-hubur brings to you. The silver passes overland in the name of ... Šu-hubur should give you x+3 minas 2⅓ shekels of silver under my seal and a certified tablet with my seal, and then you (plural) must open for my tablets, give him his tablet from Ali-ahum's (house) and place the tablet that Šu-hubur gives to you among my other tablets and seal (the box) with your seals. And the bundle should remain with Ali-ahum under my seal until I arrive. Five times I have sent word to you concerning Iddin-Aššur's silver, but you have written nothing to me to inform me. You have not sent me word to inform me whether he has paid the silver and its interest or not. If he has not paid the silver I shall write so they can make him pay the silver and its interest, and as for you, with the first transport ...

translation: To Aššur-damiq from Abu-šalim: The leatherworkers here who owe ... to Luhrahna have received the hide of an ox from the Amorites, and I am the guarantor for 1 ½ mina 5 shekels of copper. Also, they promised ... for me, (but) they have given me nothing. Here the Amorites seized (them) with you as witness. Seize them there and have them give you the copper. Illil-bāni should send me ½ mina of copper. An ax has been deposited as security.

translation: 22 minas: the house of Aššur-imittī and hunniya; 20½ minas: Ilī-ālum; 10 minas less 15 shekels: Šu-Kūbum; 13 minas: the house of Šu-Illil; 13 minas the son of Amur-Ištar; 13⅔ minas 5 shekels belonging to Lā-qēp son of Kayatum; 6½ minas: Aššur-malik son of Ennam-Adad; in all: 1½ talent 8½ minas of silver from my joint-stock capital, including the which my investors have charged to me. Of the 10 minas of silver from his in my certified tablet belonging to Šu-Kūbum son of Elāli he has received 5 minas of silver. Witnessed by his wife, by his daughter, the priestess, by Elāli, his son.

translation: Šalim-Aššur's attorney seized us against Ennam-Aššur and Ali-ahum, Šalim-Aššur's sons, and the attorney said: Your father's investors kept the tablet stating which silver your father set down as owed by you, and the investors placed it in front of the colony. The colony entrusted it to me. Come, in accordance with the tablet of the City pay the silver for which you were noted in the tablet, seal it and go to the City. Do not cheat me." Ali-ahum answered: "Come, let us pay what silver our father set down as owed by us and then let me go with the attorney." Ennam-Aššur answered the attorney: "Question me right here, and then I shall answer you and I shall leave right now." The Kanesh colony gave us for these proceedings and we gave our testimony before Aššur's dagger. Witnessed by Puzur-... son of Aššur-ṭāb, by Šu-Aššur son of Šu-Suen."

As to the ⅓ mina of silver belonging to the lady and the 17 shekels of silver belonging to Ilī-kurub, if they raise claim against Buziya, Šu-Ištar will clear him. transliteration: umma lā-lā-sí-mā ana <PN>Al-aḫim</PN> qibima ištu MU.1.ŠÈ ṭuppīka u dannātēka rābiṣum ublamma u attunu adi ūmem anniem sà-aḫ-ra-tù-nu ayyam ūmam tuqa''ā lā tallakanima bētum abīkunu lā tù-za-kà-a- u annākam līmum bētam ik-ta-na-na-ak apputtum <PN>Šuma</PN> aḫī <PN>Adā</PN> ammākam lā taštanamme kīma da-nu-tù-ni kīma abūni e-zi-bi₄-ni ukultī nu-ḫa-bu-lu-mā ni-ku-lu kaspam 1 šiqil šumē aḫī a--na-ku-ba a- <PN>Mannum</PN> dannūtum ālem kīma ṭuppī za-ište-a--nim-mā bētum iṭ-ra-a- ana be'ūlātim diššuma be-u-lā-tí raqqatam arbe i--na-mì-tim ru-pu-ša ga be im x
translation: From Lamassī to Ali-ahum: A year ago the attorney brought your tablets and your strict commands, but as for you (pl.), you have delayed until this day! Which day are you waiting for? You (plur.) do not come and clear the affairs of your paternal house, and the eponymn tries to seal up the house. Urgent, if you are truely my brother, don't you keep hearing there that conditions here are harsh? Do you not know that our father left me in an empty house, so we have to borrow money for food for the household to have something to eat? Why do you not send me a single shekel silver in my name in a shipment? If you are truly my brother - as for me, whom can I look to apart from you? Conditions are harsh in the City. Urgent, as you hear my letter, clear yourselves, set out and come and save your father's house. If Aluwa attends to you there, let him do so - or if that is not the case - hand him over for a working capital and send me the working capital . Also, he owes me 13 shekels of silver - seize him and have him pay the silver and send it. Adida brings you a thin textile, four cubits wide and ten long, under my seal. ... Adida.

translation: Thus Dān-Aššur and Ennam-Suen, say to Ir'am-Aššur: 10 textiles with the seals of Kulumāya Ennam-Aššur brought us. Two of these are Abarnian ones, one is -textile. Since there was no possibility to sell them here and these textiles are affected by moth, Ennam-Aššur brought them into Šaladuwar and he gave us 15 shekels apiece, the price made for them, and Ennam-Aššur is not on his way to you with 2½ minas of silver under our seals. Over there let Āl-ṭāb get a judicial clearance with you concerning these textiles."

translation: ... that Šalim-Aššur left behind ... let us go to the City. Yesterday I questioned you, saying: Pay the silver that your father has set down as owed by you, and then let us go to the City. Ali-ahum, your brother, answered: 'Come on, I shall pay the silver that my father wrote for me in the tablet, and then let us go to the City.' But you, instead of paying the silver keep answering me harshly, and you are unwilling to pay the silver. Do not obstruct me, but show me where your father's outstanding claims are, so I can assist you in having the silver paid, so we can go to the City. As for your brother Ali-ahum, I hold the silver that his father wrote for him in the tablet. But you, you refuse to pay the silver that your father wrote in the tablet. So you cheat me. Come, move, and pay the silver that your father wrote for you in the tablet, in accordance with the verdict of the City, and then let us go to the City. Do not obstruct me." Ennam-Aššur answered the attorney Ababa: "I submit to the tablet of the City and the attorney of my lord. Yesterday you questioned me and I answered you, saying: 'When my father died in Durhumit I was not present. My brother Ali-ahum took care of my father. They appropriated things illegally, and my father wrote many things concerning me. I do not owe any of what is in this tablet to my father. Come on, let us go to Durhumit where my father's assets are, let us take these assets and let us go together with you to the City in accordance with the verdict of the City and let us satisfy the eponym, let me discuss with my brother and my sister the testament of our father that is in the City.' If you say: 'I will not go to Durhumit,  then speak up! Come on! Even today let us depart for the City. Do not question me in court. I have not refused to go!" Ali-ahum answered the attorney Ababa; Ali-ahum said: "I submit to the tablet of the City and the attorney of my lord. Yesterday you questioned me and I answered you as follows: 'Come along! Let me pay what my father wrote in the tablet and then let us go to the City!' Come, let me pay the silver today and then let me show you my father's outstanding claims, so assist me and let us have the silver paid and go to the City in accordance with the tablet of the City. I shall not obstruct the tablet of the City and the attorney of our lord. The Kanesh colony gave us for these proceedings and we gave our testimony before Aššur's dagger. Witnessed by Uṣurānum son of Salliya, by Aššur-taklāku son of Aššur-muttabbil."

translation: To Adida and Ali-ahum from Damiq-pī-Aššur: Our own Amur-Ištar owes me 14 shekels of silver. Make him pay the silver and send it to me. Zuzuwa brings you 1 good textile. translation: When Enna-Suen was about to leave on a journey we said as follows to Aššuriš-tikal with Enna-Suen as witness: "As to the silver the matter has been concluded. The man decided otherwise and the silver was not given to us. Go to the City there and let Enna-Suen and Ali-ahum make a statement to the City, that he refuses to give the silver. translation: Say to Aššur-rēṣī, Dadiya and Ennam-Aššur, thus Elamma: Dān-Aššur is on his way to you with 24 minas of refined silver, its excise added, his transport fee paid. translation: 41 minas 11½ shekels of refined silver, sealed by your representatives and by me - in three packages; further ⅔ mina 1 shekel, its transport tariff - all this I entrusted to Šu-Nūnu and Ili-ašrannī, and they have brought it to Šalim-Aššur, our father, in accordance with his orders. Furthermore, I gave them 5 shekels of silver for their food. Witnessed by Ahu-waqar son of Zurzur, by Aššur-taklāku son of Qardum-Adad. Furthermore, I gave 10 shekels of silver for a working-capital to Šu-Nūnu. 7 shekels of silver I gave as a working-capital to Il-ašrannī witnessed by the same men.

transliteration: umma <PN>Lamassī-ma</PN> ana <PN>Ennam-Aššur</PN> u <PN>Al-aḫim</PN> qibima tašpurānem umma attunuma rābiṣam aḫ-za-nim u ṭuppam ša ālem liqeānem rābiṣam nīḫuzakkunūti u ṭuppam ša ālem nilqe ammākam kīma ša buluṭ abīkunu lā tuštēṣṣa'āma <PN>ša-li-Amurrum</PN> iṣṣēr bētum abīkunu lā išalla lu šîttam attunuma kasap abīni mala awīluttīkunu paḫirama u pūt abīni u bēt abīni e-bi-ba-mā <PN>ša-li-Amurrum</PN> iṣṣēr bēt abīni lā išalla lā tušteṣṣa'ā apputtum <PN>Šuma</PN> aḫḫūa attunu rābiṣum ēkušakkunūti kaspam 10 <PN>Mana</PN> mala awīluttīkunu lu da-pu-ur-tí bētum abīni u bētum abīni e-bu-bi-im epšāma u rāmakkunu za-ište-a--nim tib'ānemma atalkānimma u ište tamkārum u ummiānē abīkunu <PN>Zukuwa</PN> apputtum <PN>Šuma</PN> ammākam attunu šattam ištêt sà-aḫ-ra-tù-nu za-lu-ar-tám ašar 1 <PN>Mana</PN> u 2 manā'ē kaspam abūni ḫabbulu
translation: From Lamassī to Ennam-Aššur and Ali-ahum: You have written, saying: Hire an attorney for me and get hold of a tablet from the City." We have hired an attorney for you and we got hold of a tablet from the City. Just as when your father was still alive do not quarrel there so no evildoer may do harm to your father's house. As for the rest, it is you who must collect our father's silver as true gentlemen, and clear our father and our father's house of claims, and so no evildoer can do harm to our father's house you must not quarrel.Urgent, if you are truly my brothers, the attorney has gone to you - act so that you make at least 10 minas of silver as true gentlemen, by clearing both the satisfaction? of our father's house and our father's house itself, and then clear yourselves, set out and come here so that you may clear matters with the customers and investors of your father. Urgent, if you are delayed there for a single year, then send ... where our father owes 1 or 2 minas of silver, and then let us pay it. ... do not go out ..."

translation: 12 shekels of silver, the interest on 2 minas of silver, is owed by the man from Tumliya.

transliteration: ana <PN>Lamassatim</PN> u <PN>Šalimma</PN> qibima umma <PN>Umme-Išḫarama</PN> adi našpertem ša tašpurīnni umma atimma miššum <PN>Maman</PN> lā iṭarradam šiparšu illikamma anāku aṭrud adi mala u šinēšu aq-bi-šu-mā libbušu i--ta-na-aṣ-ra-áp umma šūtma adi mala u šinēšu našperti i--li-ik-šī-im-mā alākam lā tammuā ša a--ša-pá-ru-šī-ni-BA iṣṣēr našperātēa ištêt u šitta ša i--li-kà-šī-ni awīlum awâtem i--ta-aḫ-dar umma šūtma ištu alākam lā tamū' lā ta-tù-ri-mā lā ta-qá-bi-im <PN>Šuma</PN> aḫātī attī awâtem sarrātem lā ta-ṣimid-ta-na-pá-ri-im ana kaspam mimma lā <PN>ta-ša-pá-ri-šu-Amurrum</PN> aššumi kaspam aq-bi-šu-mā umma šūtma mal'amma kaspam ½ <PN>Mana</PN> gamrīša gimillam iṣṣēr ummīša ūl a--ḫi-ša laškun ūl ina ba'abtīa kaspam 10 šiqil lā ibašši u <PN>Šuma</PN> ina ba'abtīa laššu kaspam 10 šiqil mala gamrē
translation: To Lamassutum and Šalimma, thus says Ummī-Išhara: As for the letter you sent me, in which you wrote: 'Why does he not send someone to me?' a messenger of his did arrive, but it was me who sent him away. I talked to him several times, but every time he bursts out, saying: 'Several letters of mine went to her, but she refused to come here! Could what I write her (now) really surpass the messages that already reached her several times?.'The gentleman has become very annoyed by the matter and said: 'Because she refuses to come, you must not again speak to me!' If you are my sister, do not keep writing me things that are not true and certainly do not write him for silver. I talked to him because of the silver and he said: 'Should I really oblige her mother or her brothers for no less than half a mina of silver for her expenses? Are there no ten shekels of silver available from my outstanding claims? And if they are not let her ask ten shekels of silver for her expenses from her mother or her brothers, which I promise to pay back here if only she leaves for here'. Do not keep writing me all kind of things and messages. You have brought me into conflict with the gentleman. He tells me: 'Since, not being my maid, she refuses to come here, you must not mention her name to me again, lest you will no longer be my sister!' Why are others ruling your children and your household, while you are staying there? Please do not make your children perish and do not estrange me from the gentleman's house. If you see a possibility to come, get ready and leave for here, before the gentleman gets different ideas. The day Pilah-Ištar arrived here, since you had not accompanied him, he felt very unhappy and for five days did not leave his house. If you are seeking another husband, write me so, I wish to know it. If not, get ready to leave and come here. If you do not come, you will bring me into conflict with the gentleman and you will make your children perish and I, I will never again mention your name, you will no longer be my sister and you don't have to write me any more.""

translation: To ... and ... from Iddin-abum: for the 1 mina of silver for which Lamas-sutum, Anna-anna and Ab-šalim have become indebted to haššu-uman, and for which they have given him tablets belonging to our father as security, I have concluded their matter with hanunu, Šu-Ištar and Aššur-malik as witnesses, and I reimbursed him for the tablets of our father, and he has been paid, and the rest of the silver ... Pay ... to haššu-uman's son and then certify a tablet with his seal and the seals of his mother and brother, stating that I have redeemed the women and our father's tablets, and that I have personally out of my own funds paid silver to cover the debt of the women. My dear brothers and lords, take care and get hold of a strong tablet, so that not a single shekel of silver will elude me, and there give ... to my brothers ...

transliteration: umma <PN>Šu-Bēlum-ma</PN> ana <PN>Enna-Suen</PN> u <PN>Al-aḫim</PN> qibima 11 ṣubātem qadum ša ṣuḫārem u šina maškunu <PN>Zupa</PN> u <PN>Adad-bānī</PN> šattem-pá-zi-ru-u naš'ūnekkunūti 10 šiqil kaspam igrēšunu dinaššunūti u 10 šiqil kaspam xx adi šēbilā xx-bu-mā ṣuḫārum lā isaḫḫur ṭurdanni ša 1 šiqil kaspam šī-ni-in u šēnātem ša sinništem šāmamma šēbilānem apputtum ṣubātem mala tale''e'āni dinaššunu aḫḫūa attunu <PN>Lulu</PN> ṣubātem aḫiuttem uš-té-né-ra-áb u attunu ištēšu namgerāma ište ṣuḫārem ṣuḫāršu lētiqamma ṣubātem lu 50 lu lušētiqam
translation: From Šu-Bēlum to Enna-Suen and Ali-ahum: Zuba and Adad-bāni, the smugglers, bring you 11 textiles, including those belonging to the servant, and two covers. Give them their wages, 10 shekels of silver; also, send 10 shekels of silver ... and the servant must not be delayed - send him. Buy shoes for 1 shekel of silver and some shoes for women and send them. Urgent, as for the textiles, sell them as well as you can. My dear brothers, Lulu keeps having textiles belonging to strangers brought in, so you must reach an agreement with him that his servant travels here with the servant, so he may send 20 or 30 textiles here.

transliteration: 1 abarniam 1 burā'am ana <PN>Kukuzi</PN> mer'a <PN>Saḫri-ilī</PN> ša <GN>Šalatuwar</GN> ana ši'āmātem <PN>Adin</PN> aḫamma 2 <PN>Mana</PN> weri šikkam ana šēnēn šuḫuppātem damiqtem addišum
translation: I gave 1 Abarnian textile, 1 burā'u-textile to Kukuzi son of Sahri-ilī from Šalatuwar for purchases.

translation: Šalim-Aššur seized us and said to Šu-Bēlum and Enna-Suen: I have paid some 1 or 2 talents of silver for your father's debt out of my joint-stock capital. Come on, look at the tablets concerning your father's debt and pay me my silver." They said: "Our father's tablets and copies were sealed with the seals of Šu-Illil, Amur-Ištar and Šu-Anum, and they are in the City. If indeed you can establish anything as owed by our father, will you refuse to take it complete in the City?" Šalim-Aššur answered Šu-Bēlum: "I have personally promised to collect the silver that is in Anatolia. Why have you taken silver from Dada's son in hahhum?" Šu-Bēlum answered: "Yes, I took it." So he asked Enna-Suen, saying: "Why have you taken silver in Timel-kiya?" He answered: "I shall look whether I took any, but there is nothing." The Kanesh colony gave us for these proceedings and we gave our testimony before Aššur's dagger. Witnessed by Akuza, by Lalum, by Šu-Kūbum, by Aššur-imittī, by Itūr-ilī. "

Further, 2 undergarments, 4½ -textiles belonging to Anna-anna were given to Šu-Ištar for purchases.Witnessed by these men.

translation: The hahhum colony has passed a verdict: If Šu-Bēlum and Enna-Suen, Iddin-abum's sons, do not go to the Kanesh colony and do not meet with Šalim-Aššur and do not discuss in order to come to an agreement, then they must release the goods to Šalim-Aššur. Aba was the arbitrator.

translation: Hatāni and Ewarimuša brought previously 1⅓ mina 6 shekels of silver; further, 1 mina 19 shekels of silver in their second transport. They gave 1 mina of silver, the price of the first slave and the earlier ones which they conducted here. Thereof: 5 1 / 4 shekels of silver owed by the gardener Ahuašu. 1½ mina of silver and 15 shekels of interest I paid to Aššur-malik. I paid ⅚ mina to Katu. I paid ⅓ mina 5 shekels to the man from Ebla. I paid all this in the name of Amur-Šamaš. Further, Itūr-ilī took on my behalf 1 mina of silver from the price of the first slave.

translation: 4 talents 58 minas (of tin) the declared value of Šu-Ištar('s shipment), 24 minas 10 shekels (of tin), including the fodder, I paid. 6½ shekels (of tin) from the Town of the Kaneshites until Timilkiya. 2 shekels of silver and 2 shekels of tin the hire of a donkey from Timilkiya until hurama I paid. 4½ shekels of silver and 4½ shekels of tin the hire of a donkey and a donkey-driver from hurama until Kanesh I paid. All this I paid for the sake of Šu-Ištar.

transliteration: umma <PN>Šu-Bēlum-ma</PN> ana <PN>Al-aḫim</PN> qibima mala ina <GN>Kaneš</GN> unaḫḫidūkani umma anākuma allikma ina ālem aḫātī aplam lu talqeam u i- našpertēa ište aḫātīa kuāti u <PN>Nab(i)-Suen</PN> al-pu-ut-ku-nu aḫī <PN>Adā</PN> <PN>Šuma</PN> aḫātīa ina ālem aplam talqeam tîrtaka zakūtum ište <PN>Azu</PN> wābil ṭuppem lillikamma libbi liḫdû maḫar <GN>Aššur</GN> u <PN>Adad</PN> i--li-a--bi-ni lakrubakkum
translation: From Šu-Bēlum to Ali-ahum: As I instructed you in Kanesh when I said: Go and (see to it that) my sister acquires an heir for me in the City" - so I wrote in my missive to you and Nabi-Suen together with my sister. My dear brother, if my sister has acquired an heir in the City, then let an exhaustive report come here with Azu, the one who brings (this) letter, so I shall be happy. I shall pray for you to Aššur and Adad, the gods of our father."

translation: Dan-Aššur detains Enna-Suen son of Iddin-abum and he gave him to hanu son of Itūr-ilī as guarantor. Dan-Aššur said: You will return the man. If you have not returned the man you will be responsible for 12 minas of silver and its interest in accordance with the certified tablet concerning his father's debt." Enna-Suen said: "For his debt to whom?" Dan-Aššur said: "He is indebted either to my father or anonymously. But if you have a quittance, then bring it and invalidate the tablet." The Kanesh colony gave us for these proceedings and we gave our testimony before Aššur's dagger.Witnessed by Nazi, by Puzur-Anna, by Ah-šalim."

translation: From Enna-Suen to Ali-ahum: 1⅓ shekel 15 grains of gold dust, owed by Dadaya; he is to pay in Kanesh. Witnessed by Adad-bāni, by our own Amur-Ištar. Have him pay the gold there to you and let it remain there until I come. If he contests it with you, then give him a harsh talking-to.

translation: Say to Kukua, Ennam-Suen and Uṣur-ša-Aššur, thus Šu-Ištar: Keep the maid there under conrol and let her not operate in Uzinum and not affect the native Anatolian. She wrote me here as follows: 'Send (somebody) to collect the price due to me'. May dear colleagues, keep the maid there under control and cheat her by telling her: 'One will conduct you to your lord. Collect your small goods and any silver you have and then you will go to your lord with the first caravan!' And as soon as she is gathering her belongings deprive her of her garment and her head-dress and sell her to somebody from Talhat. Do not sell her to an Assyrian or to a citizen of Kanesh. Get rid of her and she shall never (again) be seen in the land of Kanesh!""

translation: From Aššur-šamšī to Ennam-Aššur: Once or twice I wrote to you, saying: Send me Aššur-rēṣī's tablet." But as for you - you do not send me word. Have I not acquired dignity for you worth just 10 shekels of silver, and have I not been able to return your favours? May Aššur and the gods of friendship be my witnesses: For that silver, for at least 5 minas of silver I was able to listen to your words and I was able to return your favours! When you hear this letter ..., the tablet ... of the servant give it to Lalūm's son so he may bring it. That is indeed gentlemanly behavior."

transliteration: umma <PN>Ikkupiya-ma</PN> ana <PN>Ennum-Aššur</PN> <PN>Lā-qēpim</PN> <PN>Iddin-abim</PN> u <PN>Adad-pilaḫ</PN> qibima 10 <PN>Mana</PN> kaspam ṣarrupam <PN>Ennum-Aššur</PN> ublakkunūti ša 2 <PN>Mana</PN> x kaspam annukum damiqtam šāmānemma aḫamma kunkāniššu ša šîttē kaspam šīmam ša balāṭīa šāmānem ana <PN>Ennum-Aššur</PN> qibima 40 <PN>Mana</PN> annukum damiqtam i- libbīka aḫī <PN>Adā</PN> annukum dammiqma ište ālikem paniēma šēbilānem aḫḫūa attunu iḫdamma ṣuḫārī lā isaḫḫur ⅓ <PN>Mana</PN> 3 šiqil kaspam ṣarrupam <PN>Susaya</PN> mer'a <PN>Šukketem</PN> ḫabbulam warḫem ša kēnātem a--30 ūmē išaqqal līmum <PN>Buzutaya</PN> ana ṣibtem illakšum ṭuppam ša šēbīa ša bāb ilum uka''al kaspam u ṣibassu šašqilāšu <PN>Šuma</PN> mimma kaspam u ṣibassu liddinakkunūtima dannassu liqbiakkunūti <PN>Šuma</PN> lā itaḫbalam ṭuppēa peteamma taḫsisātem ša šumē <PN>Erišim</PN> laptū šé
translation: From Ikūn-pīya to Ennam-Aššur, Lā-qēpum, Iddin-abum and Adad-pilah: Ennam Aššur has brought you 10 minas of refined silver. Buy good tin for 2 minas of silver and seal that seperately. For the rest of the silver make a profitable purchase for me. To Ennam-Aššur: you owe 40 minas of good tin. My dear brother, send me the tin with the first transport as a favour to me. My dear brothers, take care that my servant is not delayed. Susaya son of Šukkutum owes me ⅓ mina 3 shekels of refined silver; from the month Ša-kēnātim he is to pay in 30 days; eponymy Buzutaya. It draws interest from him. I hold the tablet with my witnesses from the Gate of the God. Make him pay the silver and its interest. If there is any silver and its interest then let him give it to you, even though he may raise objections to you. If he (pretends that he) has not become indebted to me, then open my tablets and send me the memoranda written in the name of Erišum. Place the tablet of Ikūn-pī-Ištar among my tablets and after that you four must seal. Ask Ennam-Aššur about a tablet concerning 2½ minas of silver where the creditor's name has been declared, and send it to me.

translation: Ennam-Aššur owes 5 shekels of silver to Luzi. He will bring one -textile worth 5 shekels of silver up here from the City within one year. If he has not brought a  up here from the City in one year, he must pay 10 shekels of silver here. Month Tē'inātum, eponymy Elāli, the high priest. Witnessed by Atata, by Lā-qēp.

translation: To Šalim-Aššur from Ennam-Aššur: Your representatives entered your house, opened for your tablets and took out the tablet concerning the debt of Uṣur-ša-Aššur and Aššur-ṭāb and we entrusted it to Abuwa. Now, (listen to) its copy: Puzur-Ti'amtum, Aššur-imittī son of Ataya and Uṣur-ša-Aššur ...Abuwa ... I keep writing Aššur-ṭāb son of Sadaya ... but he will not come. For how long ... and he was not afraid to speak before your representatives. Why should I write at length to you, that we are unhappy and have no one to care for us? My dear father, send a final report to your representatives and to me. I shall do what you order, and I shall clear myself and come so I can clear it with you. 4 minas 3 shekels ... lapis lazuli ... of Ennānum and ... the transport tariff for the silver ..."

translation: To Aššur-nimrī, Ali-ahum, Šamaš-bāni and Nūr-Ištar from Puzur-Anna; specifically to Šamaš-bāni: In addition to (what was in) your memo - they added 6 shekels of silver for you from after you left; 13 minas of tin under your seal and the seal of Puzur-Aššur that you left me. Witnessed by Taqin-abum, by Enna-Suen, by Iddin-Aššur son of Kuzilānum. I checked your ... for Puzur-Aššur son of Iliya, and I personally paid his 13⅔ minas at 6⅚ minas each for you. In all, 19½ minas of tin were paid. The 10 mina weighing stone by which he weighed was ⅓ mina too large. He is ready to open the packages of my investors ... Until he has made me pay the -tin, my dear brother, pay 7 shekels of silver per (mina) for my tin to my representatives. May it be a favour for me since I have done you a favour and I have arranged a caravan for you.

translation: From Kukuwa and Šu-Ištar to Ennam-Aššur: In accordance with your instuctions your representative... gave 1 mina of checked silver and ⅚ mina of refined silver to Ištar-lamassī and Mannum-kī-iliya against interest. Here Kukuwa paid 2 minas 4 shekels of silver and entrusted it to Šu-Ištar under his seal. We shall go to Kanesh and he will see the tablet with his seal, they will pay the silver and its interest to the representatives of the merchant, and we shall release their tablet. The silver will then travel overland in their name. He further paid ⅚ mina 3 shekels of silver from his valid tablet, and entrusted it under his seal to Šu-Ištar. He said: I am waiting for my surety,  so let him go to Kanesh to your representatives, so they may release his surety and his tablet. Ababa, Šalim-wardī, and Šēp-Ištar lead 15 talents of wool, 7 black donkeys and 7  to you. Have Šalim-wardī credit your goods to you there. The winter has become bad and until today they are delayed. To Ennam-Aššur from Šu-Ištar: Send your instructions to Kanesh and with respect to my copper - where it may be reached... is not in Kanesh.

translation: 10 shekels of silver I gave to Iddin-Suen, son of Ennānum.

Ṭāb-ṣill-Aššur brings you 2 3 / 4 shekels of silver. If you are indeed my lord, send me small goods with the first transport.

translation: 15 minas of washed copper is owed by Aššur-kāšid son of Ikraya.

translation: To my representatives, Ennam-Aššur and Ali-ahum from Šalim-Aššur: I am staying in Tegarama. Before I take away my goods - urgent! - before I arrive, collect every mina of silver and let it be in my house. Do not send any silver to the City. translation: To Ali-ahum from Zukuwa: Iddin-Aššur owes me 12 minas of silver; I left the certified tablet with you. After his loan came due his terms have become overdue for me by 22 weeks. If the silver and its interest has been paid, inform me about how much silver has been paid. As to the tablets concerning Anatolians that I left as well, take care to have the silver paid. translation: From Atata, Šu-Anum, Dannaya and Lamassī to Ali-ahum: In accordance with your instructions we got a tablet of the City for you; also, we hired an attorney for you. Following the verdict of the City they must release the tablet that was entrusted to Iliya son of Elāli to the attorney, and the silver from the tablet the attorney ... he who pays must assist the attorney. As one brother has made the other hear, there pay the silver that ... to the attorney, and assist the attorney and have paid the silver that is in your brother's possession, then seal it and give it to the attorney so he can bring it. Come here yourselves and discuss about the testament concerning you. Ababa is our attorney. His wages were ⅔ mina 8 shekels of silver. Damiq-pī-Aššur gave him ⅓ mina 8 shekels of silver. Give him ⅓ mina of silver there. Travel expenses and ... - give him 8 shekels of silver. Concerning the lapis lazuli that your father gave to Man-mahir, lead your witnesses there, Enna-Suen son of Uš..., ...-Aššur and their partner down to the gate of the god, certify their tablets with your testimony and seize Man-mahir for the copper and the lapis lazuli, and make him pay the price of the lapis lazuli and the copper.

translation: Seal of Adad-pilah, son of Anīnum, seal of Aššur-lamassī, son of Lā-qēp, seal of Nazi, son of Puzur-banini. 3 minas of refined silver Aššur-lamassī, son of Lā-qēp, owes to Elamma. He will pay within 24 months from the week of Elamma and Zuba. If he does not pay when his term is up, he will add as interest 1½ shekel per mina per month. Month I, eponymy of the successor of Šu-hubur. 8 minas of refined silver Šuli, son of Puzur-Abeh, owes to Elamma. He will add as interest 1½ shekel per mina per month. Eponymy of the successor of Baziya, son of Šēp-ālim. Seal of Ilī-bāni, son of Ibni-ilī, seal of Aššur-mālik, son of Puzur-Aššur, seal of Iddin-Aššur, son of Puzur-Abeh!. 4 talents 32 minas of copper from haburata Iddin-Aššur, son of Puzur-Abeh, owes to Elamma. Seal of Šu-Ištar, son of Ennam-Aššur, seal of Ikūn-mīšar, son of Ilī-dān, that Ikūn-mīšar, son of Ilī-dān, owes 8 shekels of refined silver to Elamma. He will pay when he returns from the City. Seal of Ididi, seal of Dudurum, seal of Aššur-nādā, seal of Aššur-dūrī. 2 minas 10 shekels of refined silver Aššur-dūrī owes to Elamma. He will pay within 8 weeks from the week of Ānah-ilī. If he does not pay he will add interest per mina in conformity with the rule of the colony. (Another tablet) apart from this tablet that turns up is invalid. Seal of Zuba, son of Aššur-rē'ī, seal of Šu-Ištar, son of Sūaya, seal of Balṭu-šar, son of Sukuhum. ½ mina of refined silver Balṭu-šar owes to Elamma. He will pay within 6 months from the week of Sukkallum and Kura. If he does not pay he will add an interest of 1½ shekel per mina per month. Seal of Iddin-Suen, son of Itūr-ilī, seal of Nāb-Suen, son of Abī-ilī, seal of Idnāya, son of Kutaya. 12 shekels of refined silver Iddin-Suen, son of Itūr-ilī, owes to Aššur-ṭāb. From the week of Pūšu-kēn and Ennum-Bēlum, month IV, eponymy of Aššur-idī. translation: Say to Aššur-rēṣī, Ennam-Aššur, Dadiya and Ataya, thus Elamma: Youplur said: '17 minas of copper from the price for a house-plot of Nūr-ilī is still due from Aššur-rēṣī. 8 minas of copper belonging to Ilī-bāni, son of Ibni-ilī, is due from Ataya'. Moreover, if you have collected anything of my outstanding claims, buy for itiles and send them to me. translation: To Šalim-Aššur from Ennam-Aššur: You have written, saying: The silver that you have brought out from Burušhaddum should be deposited under the seals of my representatives." As to your outstanding loans, that you wrote about, here your representatives made you lay claim to the 10½ talents of -copper, also 40 minas of (copper) from haburat, 8 black donkeys and 2 servants, i.e. the yield in silver that Salliya and Ilī-dan owed, and they have entrusted the goods to Sahri-ilī and Ennam-Aššur son of Šu-Bēlum. translation: Šalim-Aššur's attorney questioned Ennam-Aššur and Ali-ahum, Šalim-Aššur's sons: Come on, show me where the assets, your father's silver is in accordance with the tablet of the City, then I shall release it to you. Do not obstruct me. Indeed, may these men know - listen to the missive from the investors before these witnesses, and do not raise claim against Šalim-Aššur's sons. ... as much as those who settled our case ... You have cleared me with Ikūnpīya, but many investors of your father remain, so clear me with your father's investors, and I shall raise no claim against you in accordance with those who settled our case. translation: While Šalim-Aššur, Šu-Bēlum and Enna-Suen seized each other, Šu-Bēlum said to Šalim-Aššur: Why do you detain us?" Šalim-Aššur answered: "I detain you because of the debt of your father, for which I paid silver." Šu-Bēlum asked: "For how much silver do you detain us? Do you detain us for 1 talent or for 2 talents of silver?" Šalim-Aššur answered: "I detain you for either 1 or 2 talents according to the certified tablets, stating that I paid silver for the debt of your father. But including its interest it has become 5 talents of silver." Šu-Bēlum reminded us: "Keep this in mind, what was sworn by an oath by the City." The Kanesh colony gave us for these proceedings and we gave our testimony before Aššur's dagger. Witnessed by Amurrum-bāni, by Šu-Kūbum. "

Please, my fathers, seize him and make him pay the silver. If he protests and says: 'I will pay him the silver when he comes up' - he must not leave for the countryside, seize him and make him pay the silver and let one of you give him a quittance stating that his debt-note is no longer valid." translation: From Aššur-malik and Amur-Ištar to Ali-ahum: We detained Enna-Suen here, and he said: I shall go and pay the silver in compliance with my tablet in Kanesh, and I shall annul the tablet concerning my debt and the one where Innaya is the guarantor - I shall personally do it with both my tablets." translation: Thus Šāt-Tašmētim, say to Puzur-Anna and Šu-Suen: The house has been robbed and I wander around outside. Please, my brothers ,come here so that nobody will harm your paternal house. To Tūram-ilī ,son of Balṭum ,a ... garment has immediately been forwarded. Seize him there and let him give you the garment. If you do not come quickly the city will take away the sustenance." Say to Puzur-Anna and Šu-Suen ,thus Šāt-Tašmētum: 'Why that I keep ... ... ... ,but he does not give you the slave ... ... ... ... ...? If you are really my brothers let nobody harm you. If you do not send me silver for my food I shall set out and come! If you are truly my lord - take care!

translation: Say to Aššur-šamšī and Ennam-Suen, thus Āl-ṭāb. Say in particular to Aššur-šamšī: Why are youplur. writing me as follows: 'Come here, we must submit the expenditures'? The creditor keeps a check on me (because) I have to pay 1 mina of silver! How could I come while I do not even have 10 shekels of silver available? Please, my brothers, wait one month more for me. If he treats you in a violent way, yea even turns to the colony and the colony makes you appear in court, then I am with you in it! My dear father, could I hold you in contempt? You, my father, ... ... ... ... ... ...!"

translation: Aššur-šamšī and Ennam-Suen seized us and Ennam-Suen said to Aššur-šamšī: Give me the silver that accrues to me". Aššur-šamšī answered: "I will / can not give you the silver, for I have ... ... you ... ... for ... ... ". Ennam-Suen said: "Why is it me that you are... ... ... ... ... ... me? Do it to your sons!" Aššur-šamšī answered: "I will personally take your expenses for my account". In the presence of Zuba (and) of Puzur-Adad; Ali-abum, son of Zia was our colleague. For these words the Kanesh colony made us available and this tablet (with) our testimony we presented before Aššur's dagger."

translation: Thus Šu-Išhara, say to Pilah-Ištar, Uṣur-ša-Aššur and Abu-šalim, and in particular to Uṣur-ša-Aššur: 4 talents of wool, 2 black donkeys and their harness, belonging to the merchant, which I entrusted to you in the presence of witnesses, whereby I said: 'The merchandise belongs to the merchant, it must not be seized! Convert it the very day it arrives into silver and let Abu-šalim not stay around for even 5 days!' While you were not to let him stay around for 5 days you made him stay 7 months! Please, my brother, the very day you hear this tablet, you must entrust the merchandise to Pilah-Ištar and Abu-šalim so that they bring it here. Moreover, why are you treating me with contempt? If [you] are my father ... ...""

translation: To Kuziziya, Ištar-lamassī, Nāb-Suen, Anna-anna, Amur-Ištar, Šalim-wardī and Mannum-kī-iliya from Ennam-Aššur: 1 ½ mina 5 shekels of silver sealed by Kukuwa and by me, 7 donkeys and their harness - all this belonging to me, Mannum-kī-iliya brings to you. In addition to this silver that Mannum-kī-iliya brings to you, for the 3 minas of silver and its interest that Kukuwa owes to Mannum-kī-Aššur son of Puzur-Ištar, and for which he holds 20 talents of wool as security - say to my representatives: Whatever silver Ištar-lamassī and Mannum-kī-iliya ask for there, lend them silver against interest according to the rate of the colony - from which silver you have received from my outstanding claims, or silver I sent to Anna-anna under my seal, and transfer 1 mina of refined silver thereof to them, write a debt-note for Ištar-lamassī and Mannum-kī-iliya, her son, certify it with joint liability, and give the tablet to my maid so it may remain in her possession until I come. Also, you must personally assist Ištar-lamassī and Mannum-kī-iliya and pay the silver to Mannum-kī-Aššur or to Mannum-kī-Aššur's representatives, and as to the 20 talents of wool and the -stone that Mannum-kī-Aššur holds as security, when you pay the silver let him identify Mannum-kī-iliya's seal in case the wool is sealed, and then take out the tablet of the 3 minas of silver and its interest, entrust this tablet and the -stone to Ištar-lamassī. Also, when the silver is paid, set witnesses to prove that the wool is mine. Also, check the wool for Šalim-wardī and Mannum-kī-iliya, and set witnesses for them about how much wool you clear, namely that the wool and 7 donkeys belong to Ennam-Aššur; then seal the wool and entrust it under your seals together with my other goods so they may conduct it here. translation: To Ali-ahum from Puzur-Aššur: 48 good textiles, 2 ordinary textiles, 2 textiles belonging to Aššur-bēl-awātim, a free loan, 2 talents 10 minas of sealed (tin), 3 black donkeys - all this sealed by ... my representative entrusted ... I am staying in hahhum. I left for the rest of the donkeys (with) the goods but they held up the caravan. My dear brother, decide about your goods. Send me word, and I shall not delay. Send 1 mina of silver to meet me.

translation: Puzur-Aššur, son of Ikūn-pīya, Ennam-Aššur, son of Iddin-Suen, and his brother, Iddin-Ištar, son of Ah-šalim, Ištar-bāni, Maṣi-ilī Ennam-Aššur, son of Aššur-dān, Šumi-abiya - representing the sons of Kūn-ilum - collectively paid <the expenses> of bewailing them and of Ištar-lamassī's chair from the silver that was in the house of Elamma's wife. The son of Aššur-dān and Šumi-abiya sealed the pouches.

translation: In ... we settled accounts, and for x mina 14 shekels of silver that ... ...

translation: Seal of Kula brother of Šukkutum, seal of Puzur-Ti'amtum son of Ištar-pālil, seal of Ennam-Aššur son of Karria, seal of Enna-Suen son of Iddin-abum, seal of Anuli his brother. As to the goods belonging to Šalim-Aššur that were in hahhum in the house of Issu-arik, and which the sons of Iddin-abum seized - in accordance with the tablet with a verdict of the City that Kakuwa brought, Enna-Suen and Anuli must not raise claim against Šalim-Aššur with respect to these goods.

translation: To Adida, Ali-ahum, and Uku from Puzur-Aššur: Here he has been paid ⅓ mina 1 shekel of silver from what we had available, his smuggled goods plus 2 shekel of silver. Witnessed by Ilī-pilah. If he asks for more there, then let him appoint a stand-in for you and bind him over. To Uku from Puzur-Aššur: Have I not told you as follows: 'Do not delay by two days. You did not leave me my small goods, a chisel and my woollen fleeces.' If the traveling party is detained there, then give 3 shekels of silver to the guards and send Uku to me.

transliteration: umma <PN>Ikkupiya-ma</PN> ana <PN>Ibni-ilī</PN> <PN>Begā</PN> u <PN>Ennum-Aššur</PN> qibima ana <PN>Ennum-Aššur</PN> qibima 1⅔ <PN>Mana</PN> 6 šiqil kaspam ḫabbulakkum ša 1 <PN>Mana</PN> 7 šiqil kaspam u 9 šiqil aḫamma šapratim ēzibakkum 8 šiqil kaspam lu dāt <PN>Abua</PN> lu gamrum ša annākam ištēniš 1⅓ <PN>Mana</PN> 4 šiqil kaspam talqe ⅓ <PN>Mana</PN> 2 šiqil kaspam šîttē kaspīka 2½ <PN>Mana</PN> kaspam ša ḫabbulakkunni ište <PN>Aššur-bānī</PN> ušebbalakkum 1 bilat annukum ēzibakkum <PN>Šuma</PN> šīmum lā ša'im šīmam ša balāṭīa lu tēṣābē ša <GN>Ḫaḫḫim</GN> lu saptinnemma ša <GN>Talḫat</GN> aḫḫūa attunu i- šaḫāt <PN>Ennum-Aššur</PN> izzizzamma šāmānem kannikāma ište <PN>Aššur-bānī</PN> šēbilānem ana <PN>Ennum-Aššur</PN> qibima <PN>Šuma</PN> našpertum ištu ālem ublūnem ša'ilma šēbilam a- mala našpertīka <PN>Erišum</PN> ina <GN>Durḫumit</GN> ūmam urram adaggal illakamma aṣabbassu
translation: From Ikūn-pīya to Ibnī-ilī, Bekaya and Ennam-Aššur; specifically to Ennam-Aššur: I owe you 1⅔ mina 6 shekels of silver. I left surety worth 1 mina 7 shekels of silver plus 9 shekels with you. 8 shekels of silver was either Abuwa's fees or expenses here. In all you have received 1 mina 24 shekels of silver. 22 shekels of silver was the rest of your silver; 2½ minas of silver that I owe you I shall send with Aššur-bāni. I left 1 talent of copper with you. If the purchase has not been carried out, then make purchases profitable for me, either -textiles from hahhum or  from Talhat - my dear brothers, assist Ennam-Aššur in this, seal it and send it to me with Aššur-bāni. To Ennam-Aššur: Ask whether they have brought a missive from the City and send it. In accordance with your missive I expect Erišum in Durhumit today or tomorrow. When he comes, I shall seize him.

translation: Concerning 11 -textiles, belonging to Elamma, Aššur-lamassī shall confirm the liability of Ali-ahum and Amur-Ištar for Elamma within 5 months. If he does not confirm them he shall pay 25 shekels of refined silver apiece. Month VII, eponymy of Puzur-Nirah. If one has taken extra pieces in the palace, on top of the tithe on textiles, what accrues from it to Elamma will be deducted for him from his textiles of the caravan of Lā-qēp, son of Qa'atum. In the presence of Iddin-Aššur, son of B / Pususu, of Abu-šalim, son of Iddin-Erra.

transliteration: ana <PN>Ikuppiya</PN> <PN>Libbi-Ištar</PN> <PN>Al-aḫim</PN> u <PN>Aššur-mālik</PN> ana <PN>Libbi-Ištar</PN> qibima umma <PN>Puzur-Anna-ma</PN> 3 <PN>Mana</PN> kaspam nisḫāssu watar šaddu'assu šabbu ša tamkārem addinakkum ina awātīni ši'amāt ālem lu 1 manā'um ⅔ <PN>Mana</PN> lu 1 manā'um ½ <PN>Mana</PN> ana tamkārem taddan u <PN>Adā</PN> 4 <PN>Mana</PN> kaspam nisḫāssu watar šaddu'assu šabbu iāti kīma tamkārum taddanamma u anāku tamkārum ina e-lā-i--a--mā ištu ālem addanakkum aḫī <PN>Adā</PN> kaspam u ši'āmātem kaspam mala ta-na-dí-u ana ša kīma iāti dēn u <PN>Adā</PN> 4 <PN>Mana</PN> kaspam nisḫāssu watar šaddu'assu šabbu šēbilamma kaspam mala <PN>Adā</PN> taddanāni u anāku ina e-lā-i--a- kīam laddinakkum ana ša kīma iāti qibima <PN>Šuma</PN> šīmam iddanakkunūti lā ta-mā-ḫa-ra-šu u tîrtakunu lillikam
translation: To Ikūn-pīya, Libbi-Ištar, Ali-ahum and Aššur-malik; specifically to Libbi-Ištar from Puzur-Anna: I gave you 3 minas of silver, its import duty added, its transport tariff paid for, belonging to a merchant. According to our agreement you will give from the purchase in the City either ⅔ mina or ½ mina per mina to the merchant. Then, you will personally give 4 minas of silver, its import duty added, its transport tariff paid for, to me, on behalf of the merchant, and then I shall personally be the merchant; when I come up (to Anatolia) from the City I shall give it to you. My dear brother, give whatever silver and purchases you will deposit to my representatives. Also, you must personally send me 4 minas of silver, its import duty added, its transport tariff paid for, and whatever silver you give to me I shall personally give to you in this way when I come up. To my representatives: If he gives you purchased goods, do not receive them but send me word.

transliteration: umma <PN>Kuzizīya-ma</PN> u <PN>Amur-Ištar-ma</PN> ana <PN>Al-aḫim</PN> qibima ina 15 ṣubātem ša <PN>Amur-Ištar</PN> ezibu ištu <PN>Amur-Ištar</PN> itūranni 2 ṣubātem innidnu 4 ṣubātem ša <PN>Abī-Anum</PN> ušēbilanni u 4 ṣubātem kuā'ūtem ištēniš 8 ṣubātem i- libbīa miššu ša ana 6 ṣubātem ša <PN>Abī-Anim</PN> ša tašpuranni allān 4 ṣubātem ša ušēbilanni mimma watram lā ušēbilam u adīni 2 ṣubātem šimāssu ibaššiu ammākam <PN>Alua</PN> ša'il ša ṣubātem ublanni ši'im 4 ṣubātem ša <PN>Abī-Anim</PN> u ši'im kuā'ūtem <PN>Šuma</PN> awīlū ina sikkatem wašbu ina erābīšunu lu … lu šāptem e-ba-… ušebbalakkum … ṣubātīka 12 … ina kunuk … <PN>Bēlum-bānī</PN> ibaššiu ina ṣubātem anniūtem mimma <PN>Amur-Ištar</PN> ula ilqe
translation: From Kuziziya and Amur-Ištar to Ali-ahum: Of the 15 textiles that Amur-Ištar left behind tow textiles have been sold after Amur-Ištar returned. 4 textiles that Abī-Anum sent and your own 4 textiles: in all 8 textiles are in my possession. Why is it that as for the 6 textiles belonging to Abī-Anum that you wrote about, apart from the 4 textiles he sent he as not sent anything else? So, until now the 2 textiles agreed by him are (still) outstanding. Ask Aluwa there, who brought the textiles, about the price of Abī-Anum's 4 textiles and that of yours. If the men are staying in the sikkātum, then when they arrive I shall send you both ... and the wool ... ... of your 12 textiles ... are present under Bēlum-bāni's seal. Amur-Ištar has not taken any of these textiles.

translation: 3 cups and toggle pins, their weight in silver 1 mina, under my seals; separately 26! shekels of silver also under my seals, of Elamma; 2 tablets of 2 minas 15 shekels of silver, being in the debt of the Anatolian; 1 tablet of 1½ mina of silver, being the debt of Naniya; 1 tablet of 1 mina and 6 shekels of silver, being the debt of Būr-Suen; 1 tablet of 24 shekels of silver being the debt of Ilī-tappā; 1 mina of silver (that) I gave to Ir'am-Aššur for making purchases; 1 mina of silver (that) I gave to Ah-šalim for making purchases. 9 -textiles and 1 Abarnian one, (which) I gave to Pilah-Ištar for making purchases. 5 slaves and 5 slave-girls, of whom 1 slave-girl, named Iyantalga, is for Ilina, daughter of Aššur-ṭāb. All this, Lamassutum, the wife of Elamma, left behind. Ištar-pālil, Ennam-Suen and Maṣi-ilī, Lamassutum's representative(s), will entrust it to an affiliated trader and to her sons and they will bring it to the City and (there) my daughter, the -priestess, and my sons will act in accordance with the testamentary dispositions applying to them.

translation: To Adad-bāni ..., Iliš-takil ... and Pilah-Ištar from the merchant: Pilah-Ištar and Uzuwa bring you 1 talent 35 minas of silver, its import duty added, its transport tariff paid for. My dear brothers, buy tin of extra-fine quality according to the market price and ... Pilah-Ištar brings you x fine -gold belonging to us jointly. My dear brothers, dispatch my goods with the first leaving caravan. Also, I further entrusted 40 minas of refined silver in the name of our father's house to Pilah-Ištar. Witnessed by Pūšu-kēn, by Kuziziya, by Adad-rē'ī.

translation: From Ennam-Aššur to Ali-ahum: Here 2 men have reached an agreement with me concerning our father's investors, that I shall place half of the silver before him, and it will go twice to the City and they will satisfy themselves with their silver. Concerning 3½ minas of silver that our father took on Uṣur-ša-Ištar's account in the City - for that we are pardoned. The matter will fail, and within 5 days ... and I shall send the donkeys with ... Then you too must be cleared there. Convert bad copper to good. Urgent! Do not listen to others all the time. Why is it that I keep hearing that you always listen to what strangers say? Urgent! Do not act rashly.

transliteration: 3 <PN>Mana</PN> kaspam ṣarrupam ina ši'im šāpātem ša <PN>Ušinalam</PN> <PN>Ili-ašranni</PN> mer'a <PN>Sukkallīya</PN> ilqe maḫar <PN>Aššur-bānī</PN> mer'a <PN>Kurbiā</PN> maḫar <PN>Išme-ilī</PN> maḫar <PN>Iddin-Kūbem</PN>
translation: Ilī-ašrannī son of Sukkalliya has received 3 minas of refined silver from the proceeds of Ušinalam's wool. Witnessed by Aššur-bāni son of Kurbiya, by Išme-ilum, by Iddin-Kūbum.

translation: Šalim-Aššur made us approach Amur-Ištar and Šalim-Aššur said: "Why have you taken the proceeds from 10 kutānu-textiles that I sold in the Durhumit colony?" Amur-Ištar said: "Yes, I have taken 4 talents of copper of poor quality." Šalim-Aššur said: "I hold nothing, yet you have taken it." Amur-Ištar said: "It is not you who have taken my merchandise?" Šalim-Aššur answered: "I have taken none of your merchandise." Amur-Ištar then said: "Wait until the slave has come here." Šalim-Aššur said: "Sure, let him come. Then it will be me you can pressure on the basis of what your own slave says." "Do wait!" Indeed he (may say) this; “Aššur-nadd dhas a lot of money, and that is why I cannot save my life”, or he (may say) this to the kārum; “I will produce the tablet concerning the quantity of merchandise he holds and see! " (To the extent) that the kārum does not grant him this favor, he will go to Burušhattum. The day you learn of my ta- blette, set out and come here with lli-ašranni, and from 160. The person responsible for the caravan Among the various intermediaries in whose hands the goods pass, one, designated by the expression sep NP as responsible for the goods, is responsible for organizing their transport to Kaniš. translation: To Pilaha from Irma-Aššur: thus Enlil-bâni. Kukkulânum brings you 30 silver mines — entrance fees extra, consignment tax paid—, to my seal and that of Kukkuldnum. I have rights to the silver. Here, in the house of the creditor-tamakdrum, I have been registered as guarantor of Kukkuldnum, and I have laid my hands on the 30 silver mines. 1 s-20There, stand by Kukkuldnum; let him buy with half the silver the fabrics and with (the other) half, tin according to what he deems profitable for him. Seal (the goods) and entrust them to Kuk- kuldnum with your seal. You are my brothers. Just as I have here placed my hand on the money, there at the city gate, so do you, as my representatives, place your hand on the goods, entrust them to Kukkuldnum, so that Kukkuldnum may bring the goods to me.

translation: Thus Imdilum, Ennum-Bélum and Aššur-sulû- li: say to Puzur-Aššur. We have deposited your 50 clothes-kutânum in the charge of tamkârum agents at the rate of 15 shekels (of silver) each. We will send a hundred cloth-kutanum and 4 donkeys with S1i-Bélum to Wahsušana for purchases, and we will send Iddin-Adad with S1i-Bélum. On your evening, he will receive in money the price of your hundred fabrics that Sû-Bélum brings to Wahšušana. As for the rest of your fabrics, we will deposit them for a period of 20 weeks in the charge of trusted agents for whom you will not have to worry about your money. In addition, we will enter the amount of money we have deposited with the tamkârum-agents as well as the names of your tamkârum-agents, and then our precise report will reach you. The orders of the kārum are strict, therefore for your smuggled goods about which you wrote to us, the time is not appropriate, and that why Also we will not write to you about your smuggled goods. Then, as there, the orders of the palace are strict, <and> the guards are informed (of this), I was afraid, and I said this; “My father is in a delicate position, and the palace watches over my father's house! No package must be spotted in the caravan, lest I make my father guilty of a terrible crime, my father's house suffer damage, and the palace strike my father hard. translation: Tell my donors, Sn-Hubur and my representatives: thus Pnu-kén. I asked the god for a term of 3 years in these terms; “Allow that I leave in order to clear my property- bûlâtuma and to lay before them (the donors) everything that there is. " Sil-Hubur offered me a term of 5 years, and you agreed. But I didn't agree, saying; "I don't want to wait 5 years!" I will complete the term that I asked of the god and I will release my bûlâtum property. " I6-26Two or three of my tamkârum agents on whom I depend have no common sense. A large quantity of money escaped my hands. It is however not appropriate to reveal their names to you! I (said to myself) this; “Soon they will come, the agent-tamkârum will deliver them money and they will bring me as much as possible. " 26-39Let Aššur and your god be witnesses. I was deprived of 1 or even 2 talents (of tin). That's enough! You are my masters. Please consider the number of entrance fees that can be collected in the house of my donors, then certify for me a memorandum that my capital maškattum will be used for 3 years and the money will not be seized. Then send your favorable response through my servant so that I can collect every shekel of silver from my bûlâtum possessions [and send it to you] at the latest at harvest time.

translation: Thus Sillalabum and Elàl: tell Puzur-Aššur, Amua and Aššur-Samši. Although you left the City (of Aššur) thirty years ago, and never deposited anything, and ourselves have not taken a single shekel of your money, we We never blamed you! From caravan to caravan, our tablets have reached you, but never a single letter from you has arrived here! 16-22 We have complained to your father, but (we swear that) we have no claim on your money, even for a single shekel! So please get on your way and come. Even if by chance you are delayed because of your goods sold on credit, put money at your disposal. We have never blamed you, and yet in your eyes, we are not gentlemen! Please get on your way and come, or put up some money. Otherwise, we will send a tablet from the princeb and a lawyer-râbisurnc, and we will shame you in the kârurn; As for you, you will become like someone who is no longer our brother!

translation: To Ikuppi-Aššur from Sn-Ištar: Thus Inbi-Ištar. I have left in trust in Ikuppi-Aššur and Aššur-malik, son of Kurara, 1 talent 12 mines of silver and 1 talent pewter to my seal. In addition, Aššur-malik owes me 30 silver mines from the capital-rnaskatturn, he will pay me when he comes up from the City (of Aššur). Furthermore, he is carrying 7 silver mines for me to the address of ..., and Ukuri and Warad-Knbi are carrying a copy of the memoranda relating to my witnesses. You are my brothers. The day you read my messages, certify (on a tablet the testimonies) of the witnesses of these two transactions. My money must not be lost. Once you have certified (on a tablet the testimonies) of the witnesses, intervene and seize the money, the tablets and the goods on credit where the money of Aššur-malik is located. In addition, I had given 1 min 6 shekels of silver to Samaš-tappa i as counter-value in the name of Ma- rithum. In front of Aššur-rabi and Aššur-tappa-wédim. Here o didn't give me any money. translation: Thus Sn-Hubur and the sons of Aššur-imitti: to Buzutâya, Pnšu-kén and Imdilum. If there you find that the man has power, he must not do harm to the house of our father. As you can, impose payment on him in money of the goods, because the money must be paid according to contract to the City (of Aššur). Otherwise, release the man (from his financial obligations). We keep hearing that the man is sick297! Be sure to release him (from his financial obligations). In addition, among his goods, (there are) 15 tin mines from my votive offerings. When I deposited his merchandise as his share, Aššur-ré'i, Ha- nunu and Aššur-imitti, son of Ikuppiya, gave him 5 mines of tin298. Make him pay the price of my tin. BIBLIOGRAPHY. translation: Thus Aššur-idi: tell Aššur-nâda. left me 3 3 silver mines. 1 mine 2 shekels of silver comes from Sü-Ištar. You sent me 1 mina 59 2 shekels of silver by Ištar-pilah. Dan-Aššur brought me 1 min of fine silver. In total, (there are) 8 mines. Of this amount, Aššur-nâda, son of Irnuid, sent for you merchandise amounting to 2 mines 16 shekels 112 2 grains; I also gave him the salary of the donkey driver namely 2 4 shekels. 2 shekels of silver to SU-Sin, 4 2 shekels to As- qudiya, I gave them to them, they have the obligation to pay. . If they have nothing in your account, they will have to make you a compensatory payment of 16 shekels of tin per (silver shekel). Likewise, for everything you left me left over with Aššur-ré'i, he is obliged to pay 16 shekels of tin<per (shekel of silver)>, seize it and make him pay it. Once the price of the copper as well as the shekel and the 15 grains of silver that he owed you have been paid, I repaid to Aššur-ré'i 23 shekels 22 2 grains of silver and I paid 3 mina of silver, the price of the donkey to Usur-ša-Aššur. The day you left, you took 5 mina of scrap (of metal), their price amounts to 4 shekels; the export tax at 2 shekel 15 grains. You wrote to me about this and I added it. 5 2 silver mines from the Ennum-Aššur transport; 3 shekels of silver were missing when it was checked, and I forgot to charge them to you at the time (of the balance) of the accounts. sheep from the son of Pedâya; 5 2 mines (of copper), 1 sheep; 1 s mine, from Iddin-ilim, 1 sheep; 3 mines, 1 sheep; 2 3 mines 5 shekels, 1 sheep; 2 mina 10 shekels from Aššur-ré['i], 1 sheep; 2 3 mina from Zua, 1 sheep; 2 mina from Tuliya, 1 sheep; 3 3 mina from the eldest son of the same Tuliya. You forgot 1 cloth, or 8 3 mines, from Aššur-tab, and I paid for it. In total (that's it).

translation: Thus Asšur-idi: tell Asšur-nâ,dd. You came, and five or six times you broke (your word given to the gods)! Then the weapons of Agšur and Assuritum have struck you, because you have broken (your word). You (had however said) this; “Let us point the finger at the one (who has enough disregard) for divine words to consider them as simple human wordsb! " 11-17You haven't left yet! You want to use your child to reach (...)c. You were afraid of me because I languish out of compassion for this same child! 17-22Asšur and Assuritum never cease to warn you by proclaiming; “He dispenses evil in his heart! He is not just towards you, he has committed a crime! " 23 1 Of all the orders that the gods have given you, you have clearly forgotten the words concerning our family! Indeed the gods said this; "He refuses to hear our.

translation: Thus Asssur-idi: tell Asssur-nâ,dâ,. 3—'°Why did you write me this; “You promised me that I could pay (the balance of) my accounts with your money! " I did not promise you, but you begged me, and I offered you 20 kutânum cloths in front of Asssur-kasid. "-23Since our deal has been concluded, send me the money quickly, either on the price of the cloths, or on the price of the donkeys, (for a total) of 10 mina. I will buy 2 talents of tin and I will send them to you; you must not spend any of my money. Do as you wish or not. I raised your son, but he said this to me; “You are not my father!”.

translation: Thus Assur-idi: tell Asšur-nâda. You sent me 10 silver mines. Thereupon, 2 ta- lent 10 mines of tin sealed at a rate of 16 â shekels (of tin) for one (silver shekel), its price in silver (amounts to) 7 mines 52 3 shekels; 4 fabrics-širnm and 5 fabrics- kutânv,m cost â mi[ne] silver; 7 centuries were missing when washing the argenta. translation: To Aššur-idi from Aššur-nâdâ. You are my father: “Go to your father! But who knows if the father is as good as his reputation says? " (In fact) things are going well for you! You have.

translation: Thus Aššur-idi: tell Aššur-nâdâ. I owe a solar disk [of] 15 shekels of gold to the god Ilabrat. [E]fore, when [you] came, I (said to you) this; “Why didn't you bring me the solar disk? " And you (answered me); "15 shekels, that is not enough! " So I (told you) this; “Make a purchase and convert it, then, when you arrive, make a solar disk of 15 shekels and send it to me! " i6-26Since your previous trip, you have continued to delay everything, why do you still keep the vo- tive offerings? Make sure you make the solar disk and send it to me first (departing caravan). And if the surplus has increased by some sixty centuries, then let it fall! 26-42As for my fabrics from the votive offerings of the god Aššur, how come they have not arrived? Until now, they have not been sold. Ili-äLUM and Aššur-taklâku have dyed my 190 fabrics for you', in whose house is their amount of money?

transliteration: ana <PN>Aššur-nādā</PN> qibima umma <PN>Ili-ālum-ma</PN> ina ṭuppīka 72 {TÚG}ku-ta-nu laptū lāma né-ru-ba-ni nimnušunu-ma 71 ṣubātem 1 ṣubātem batiq ina qerbemma 2 {TÚG}a-bar-ni-u aššumi nikkassēka šaḫātim am-ḫu-ur-šu-nu-mā umma šunuma ula išaḫḫat izzāz qātam liškun miššu ša umma attāma ašar pá-na-i--a- ašapparakkum <PN>Šuma</PN> attāma ana <GN>Burušḫaddem</GN> ḫa-ra-kà-mā weri-i--ni ana kaspam tutâr u anāku annākam ṣubātīka ku-ba-ri <PN>Šuma</PN> ammākam tagammil ṣubātīka ezibma ana <GN>Burušḫaddem</GN> weri-i--ni ušērrab <PN>Šuma</PN> rēš daš'ē ištên i- barēni lā ērub nēmalam ula nirašši 27⅓ <PN>Mana</PN> 5 šiqil kaspam ṣarrupam <PN>Amur-Aššur</PN> <PN>Iddin-abum</PN> ana abīni ḫabbulu kaspam šašqilma ana abīni šēbil <PN>Šuma</PN> umma <PN>Amur-Aššur-ma</PN> qātē liqe lā tamaḫḫaršu kaspam ina qaqqad šalmīšunu rakis <PN>Šuma</PN> mala ṭuppīšunu išaqqal liqe <PN>Šuma</PN> lā išaqqalakkum umma attāma mala ṭuppīkunu ṣibtam nimanû šēbē šukuššum u mala ipulūka šupram ṣubātem paniūtum lu kuā'ūtum lu iā'ūtum ša ana <PN>Elamma</PN> ezibu adīni ibaššiu warkiūtum sāsam laptū
translation: Tell Aššur-nadâ: thus Ili-aLUM. On your tablet, 72 kutânum fabrics are inscribed. Before we entered, we counted them, and (there were) 71 fabrics; so one fabric is missing! In there, (there are) 2 Abarnian fabrics. I spoke to them about the clearance of your account, and they (told me) this; “He must not clear it. He must be available; let him deposit a share! " 10-22Why did you this; “I will write to you wherever I go”? If you go to Burušhattum, then you will sell our copper for money, and I will examine your fabrics here. If you hear there that I left your fabrics, (it is) because I want to bring our copper into Burušhattum. If, at the beginning of spring, none of us entered 1 into Burušhattum), then we will not have been able to take any profit. Amur-ASSur <and> Iddin-abum owe 27 3 minas 5 shekels <of silver> to my father. Pay the money and send it to our father. If Amur-Aššur (tells you) this; “Take my share! " Do not accept this from him, because they are jointly responsible for the money. If he pays the amount for their tablet, then take it! If he doesn't pay you, you will tell him this; "We will calculate the interest according to your tab! " Place witnesses against him, and write to me what he will answer. The previous fabrics - yours or mine - that I left in Elamma, until now, they are available. (Those that arrived) subsequently are infested with moths.

transliteration: umma <PN>Puzur-Suen</PN> <PN>Alulā</PN> <PN>Būr-Aššur</PN> <PN>Šu-Ištar</PN> <PN>Lā-qēpumma</PN> ana <PN>Puzur-Aššur</PN> qibima 2½ bilat <gap> <PN>Mana</PN> annukum 1 mi'at kutānū qadum <gap> 14 {TÚG}ku-ta-nu damiqtam 10 ṣubātem ša akkadiē 4 ṣubātem ša akkadiē ša tamkārū 7 emārum ṣallāmū mimma anniem <PN>Lā-qēpum</PN> irdeam annakka nusanniqma 3 <PN>Mana</PN> annukum imṭi annakka u ṣubātīka niddanma <PN>Lā-qēpum</PN> niṭarradam annakka ša tadānim taddin ana mer'a ummiānem <PN>Kenim</PN> lā ša šaḫātim
translation: Thus Aššur-idi: tell Aššur-nacla and Assur- taklâku. I handed over (to Sarra-Adad) 2 talents 10 mines dof sealed tin, 2 black donkeys, 30 cloths-kutdnu, 4 cloths- šiiran of heavy packing and 17 mines of tin for his current expenses. A fine cloth, a cloth from Tatûr-ališša, a cloth from Ilušu-rabi — all this, Sârra-Adad has brought it to you. Tell Aššur-taklàku. Put this merchandise up for sale, and, if you are my brother, send me the money by the first traveler (to leave). Don't disappoint me. Please send me the corresponding amount personally. kutânuîn fabrics, a black donkey, 5 tin mines.

transliteration: umma <PN>Aššur-idī-ma</PN> ana <PN>Aššur-nādā</PN> <PN>Ili-ālim</PN> u <PN>Aššur-taklāku</PN> qibima miššu ša aḫūkunu ištu 2 šanat marṣūma u ta-ta-ga-lā-šu-ni apputtum inūmim ša ṭuppam tašammeāni šu-pu-ra-mā littalkam 20 <PN>Mana</PN> kaspam <PN>Ili-ālim</PN> li-ik-nu-warḫum u 8 mā-an kaspam aḫamma ša mānaḫtī bētem ša ḫabbulu lušēbilam u <PN>Aššur-nādā</PN> mala ikaššudu liknukma lušēbilam ina paniemma ālikem <PN>Aššur-taklāku</PN> ṭurdānim i- daš'ē <PN>Ilī-ālum</PN> lūṣ'am ana <PN>Aššur-nādā</PN> qibima 11 <PN>Mana</PN> annukum ša <PN>Al-aḫim</PN> i- maṣṣartem tamši-ma tēzib ište ālikē nu-šé-ba-lā-šu <gap> annukum u ⅔ <PN>Mana</PN> ḫurāṣum <big_gap> kīma 10 <PN>Mana</PN> annukum a- qātīa
translation: Thus Aššur-idi: tell Aššur-nâdâ, lli-âLUM and Aššur-taklâku. 5—11-How is it that your brother has been ill for 2 years, and you continue to trust him? Please, as soon as you read this letter, write so that he comes. Il1.-âLUM must seal 20 silver mines. As for the 8 silver mines which are also due for the maintenance of the house, let him send them. And whatever Aššur-nâdâ ogets, let him seal it and send it to me. Send me Aššur- taklâku with the next departing traveler. Let IlT-âLUM leave in the spring. Tell Aššur-nâdâ. You mistakenly left 11 tin mines from Alâhum in the safe. We will send them to him by a traveler. 30[+x mines] of tin and 3 mines of gold belong to me. 6.1.6. Iddin-Istar, the grandson Iddin-Ištar, son of Aššur-nâdâ, after leaving his grandfather's house in Aššur, hardly has any contact with him anymore. Aššur-idi accuses his grandson of having fraudulently entered his house to steal the equivalent of 3 silver mines . Iddin-Ištar then settles in Durhumit where his father visits him . He sells the latter's goods and invests the capital in the copper trade ; for this he goes to Burušhattum and Wahšušana when the political situation allows him . Iddin-Ištar defends his father's interests and property against his uncle lli-âLUM with whom he is in contact. In any case, his copper transactions are not always very successful !

transliteration: ana <PN>Aššur-nādā</PN> qibima umma <PN>Idī-Ištar-ma</PN> ištu ana <GN>Durḫumit</GN> errubū 10 bilat weri ina ba'abtīka amḫur šîttē ba'abtīka ana 20 ūmē uzakkama ana damiqtam uta''ar emārū u ilē šēriamma weri damiqtam paniamma ša ukannu ašar malākem milik ašammema weri ina <GN>Burušḫaddem</GN> ṭāb <gap> bilat 20 <PN>Mana</PN> annukum ša i- <PN>Libbiā</PN> ibašši umma <PN>Ili-ālum-ma</PN> ana <GN>Burušḫaddem</GN> lušērib umma anākuma balum tîrtī awīlem lā tù-šé-ra-áb umma šūtma <PN>Šuma</PN> annukum ša abīka lā taddanam ša <PN>Al-aḫim</PN> dinamma <PN>Al-aḫam</PN> lagmil umma anākuma tîrtum libbalkitam 10 bilat weri i--šī-im annukum alqema ibašši werîka 20 bilat nadi 2 ṭuppē ṣuḫārum ša <PN>Aššur-imittī</PN> ublakkum ši'āmātēka uzakkama ana <GN>Burušḫaddum</GN> errab anne ammākam a- tîrtīka uqa''a
translation: Tell Aššur-nâda: thus Iddin-Ištar. Since I arrived in Durhumit, I have received 10 talents of copper from your goods sold on credit. I will clear the rest of your goods on credit within 20 days, and convert them for good quality copper. I've had some donkeys brought in, so make a decision on the very first good quality copper I get. I learn that copper is of good quality in Burušhattum. There are [x] talents 20 tin mines in my account. Here is what lli-äLUM said; “I will bring it into Burušhattum! " I (answered him) like this; “I can't let him in without instructions from the man!” " He then said this; “If you cannot give me your father's tin, then give me Alâhum's so that I may render service to Alâhum. " I (answered him) like this; “Let the goods pass! "28-36 I took 10 talents of copper from the amount of tin, and it is available. In total, 20 copper talents belonging to you are deposited. Aššur- imitti's servant brings you 2 tablets. I will clear your purchases and enter Burušhattum. Now, there, I will wait for your instructions.

transliteration: ana <PN>Innā</PN> qibima umma <PN>Abāma</PN> 3 kutānū <PN>Apatanānum</PN> naš'akkum 1 ṣubātem kabtam <PN>Šumi-abiā</PN> naš'akkum bētum aḫīka attāma tīde kīma 1 šiqil kaspam ašar laqā'em lā ibaššiu mīnam ana 10 <PN>Mana</PN> kaspam annēšam taštanappar iḫidma kaspam ammākam liqema ina alākīka ṣulum pani lā tukallamāni <PN>Šuma</PN> bēlī <PN>Adā</PN> kaspam ša <PN>Puzur-Suen</PN> ša ilqeu lā igammarma iḫid kasapka ammākamma liqe ina ša ištēšu batiqtam u watartam a--lā-pá-ta-ku-ni libbaka lā ilammin umma anākuma adi liḫḫidma kaspam liddinakkumma ḫimṭātem u-lā-pī-tám mīnam šazzuztīka lašpur ammākam attāma ša'il
translation: Tell Innâya: thus Abâya. Apatananum brings you 3 clothes-kutdnum. Sumi- abIya brings you 1 heavy cloth. Regarding your brother's house, you know very well that there is no money, even a shekel, where (we could) take some. why, do you keep writing to me here (in Aššur) for 10 minae of silver? Make sure you take the money there. Well, when you arrive, don't show me an angry face! 17-27If you are my master, the money that Puzur-Sîn took, he must not spend it, so be sure to take your money there. You must not get angry because I am going to record for you with him what is plus or minus (in the accounts). translation: Tell Innâya: thus Tarâm-Kubi. You wrote this to me; a Keep the bracelets and rings that are here, that they serve for your food. " In reality, you made me wear 2 gold mines by Ili-bâni.
